messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhang <emma@edgeware.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Monthly commit checkpoint & PO lanes

Thanks for taking time today, Emma — good conversation. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can line up procurement:

- Use case: model embeddings + chat for clinical triage (low-latency, bursty daytime traffic).
- Token profile we discussed: ~250M tokens/month projected at steady state, with early pilot months closer to 40–80M.
- Questions for you to confirm:
  1) Target monthly spend band you want us to qualify for the procurement team (e.g., $10k-$30k, $30k-$60k).
  2) Your PO threshold (minimum monthly amount that triggers a formal PO/invoice cadence).
  3) Target $/1M tokens you're comfortable with as a benchmark (you mentioned internal target ranges during the call).

Next steps I propose: I can draft two simple procurement lanes we typically use (self-serve invoice for < $X, reserved monthly commit + PO for >= $X) and send a short matrix comparing unit economics across bands. I attached our latest pricing grid (redwood-pricing-grid-v2.pdf) for reference.

Are you able to share Edgeware's PO threshold and preferred invoice timing (Net 30/45)? If you want, copy your procurement contact and I can loop them in.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: redwood-pricing-grid-v2.pdf (pricing matrix, 3 pages)

From: Emma Zhang <emma@edgeware.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@edgeware.com, Oliver Lang <oliver.lang@edgeware.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Monthly commit checkpoint & PO lanes

Thanks, Mateo — good summary. A few clarifications from our side after looping in procurement:

- Monthly spend band we expect to qualify against: our initial pilot months are ~15k–25k/mo; production target in 6–9 months is 35k–60k/mo.
- Edgeware's procurement threshold for vendor-managed POs is $20k/month. Anything below that goes through our AP team as standard invoices.
- For unit economics, our internal target is roughly $1,000–$1,300 per 1M tokens (we're modeling conservatively today).
- Invoice timing: procurement prefers Net 30 once a PO is in place. For invoices under $20k we can pay Net 15 through AP.

We attached our vendor purchase policy for reference (edgeware-purchase-policy.pdf). Happy for you to draft the two lanes — once we see proposed bands we'll confirm whether we can commit to a rolling monthly reserve or prefer pay-as-you-go for the pilot.

Best,
Emma Zhang
Head of Product Operations | Edgeware Health
emma@edgeware.com

Attachment: edgeware-purchase-policy.pdf (procurement thresholds and AP routing)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Monthly commit checkpoint & PO lanes

Forwarding Emma's note — procurement threshold is $20k/mo and their target unit econ is $1k-$1.3k per 1M. Pilot months ~15k–25k, ramp to 35k–60k.

Thinking aloud: we should present two concrete lanes:
- Lane A (pilot / low commitment): pay-as-you-go invoices, no PO required for < $20k/mo, unit price = list (no commit discount).
- Lane B (commit lane / PO): for >= $20k/mo, offer a modest commit discount tied to a 3-month rolling reserve or monthly commit with 30-day PO terms. Suggesting starting pricing for Lane B around $1,100/1M for the 20–40k band, and $950/1M for >40k.

Questions for you both:
1) Is the >40k tier at $950 defensible from margin/exec perspective?
2) Should we allow a split-invoice option (monthly PO for committed portion + usage invoice for overage)? That might help procurement accept a lower commit.

I'll draft a quick CSV matrix (proposed-commit-matrix.csv) and send to Emma once we align.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhang <emma@edgeware.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, procurement@edgeware.com
Date: Fri, 6 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Monthly commit checkpoint & PO lanes

Emma — appreciate the clarity. Quick proposal from our side to make procurement simple and keep your pilot flexible:

Proposal (high level):
- Pilot lane (<= $20k/mo): pay-as-you-go invoices, Net 15, no PO required. Unit price = $1,300 / 1M tokens (matches your conservative model).
- Commit lane (>= $20k/mo): 30-day PO, monthly reserved commit with a 3-month rolling minimum. Pricing tiers: $1,100 / 1M tokens for $20k–$40k band, $950 / 1M tokens for >$40k band. Overage billing at list price.
- Splitting invoices: we can accept split invoicing for customers who want a PO only on the committed portion; usage overage will be invoiced separately.

If the above looks reasonable we can generate a short SOW + billing addendum and route to your procurement contact for DocuSign. If you'd like, we can also include a 30-day trial credit against overage for the pilot months to reduce switching risk.

Next step: Emma — confirm whether procurement wants the commit to be expressed as dollar value (e.g., $25k/month) or token units in the PO. We typically recommend dollars for simplicity but can express both.

I'll attach the proposed-commit-matrix.csv with the bands and back-of-envelope unit economics.

— Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Attachment: proposed-commit-matrix.csv (simple band matrix)
